# Review pack: review-observability

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-observability.<language>.md`. ## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Observability

Assesses the telemetry that application code and app configuration emit (logs, traces, metrics, resource identity,
error recording), the health endpoints the app exposes, and SLO/SLI documentation. It uses local, pinned summaries
of OpenTelemetry and the Azure Well-Architected Framework. Alert rules, dashboards, external probes and telemetry
routing in IaC are reviewed by `review-monitoring`.

#### Inputs

Logging, tracing and metrics setup, OpenTelemetry or APM SDK configuration and agent settings, exception handling
middleware, health check endpoints and probe manifests, SLO docs, per `compliance-inventory`.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/opentelemetry-observability.md` — OTO-01…OTO-46. Always load.
- `references/standards/azure-well-architected-observability.md` — WAFO-01…WAFO-37. Always load.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, both standards files, and
   `references/languages/<id>.md` for each detected language.
2. Service type: classify the target (web/API service, worker/consumer, library, CLI/batch, front-end only). OBS-06
   applies only to long-running deployable services. Cross-service parts of OBS-02/OBS-03 apply only when the code
   calls or receives calls from other services, databases or brokers. For a library, judge only OTO-13, OTO-15 and
   the absence of SDK/exporter setup, and mark OBS-05 N/A.
3. Instrumentation mode (language file signals): zero-code agent, code-based SDK, vendor APM SDK, or none.
   Zero-code configured for the service passes framework tracing and HTTP metrics (OTO-14, OTO-23); custom spans and
   business metrics (OTO-16, WAFO-08) are still judged on code. A vendor SDK is "equivalent" for OBS-03…OBS-05; skip
   OpenTelemetry naming elements (OTO-18…OTO-21, OTO-31…OTO-36) unless it uses OpenTelemetry conventions, with reason
   "vendor SDK; OpenTelemetry naming not applicable".
4. For each check (OBS-01…OBS-10), evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when" condition holds. If none
   apply, mark the check N/A with that reason.
5. Development-status elements (Stab. `D`): apply when the repo already uses that convention; otherwise report only
   as confidence `low`.
6. Boundaries: don't report alert rules, dashboards, external probes, probe thresholds or telemetry retention
   (review-monitoring); routing and restart probe configuration (review-reliability AZRL-49/50); secrets/PII in log messages, log injection or security-event logging (security skills; if
   both could fire on the same line, don't report it here); API header documentation (review-api-design).
   OBS-10 covers only telemetry attributes, baggage and captured headers/bodies. OBS-07 is the only place a missing
   SLO is reported.
7. OBS-06: the endpoint must exist and be wired to the host's probe mechanism when manifests are in scope. A
   constant-200 handler passes WAFO-14 but fails WAFO-16 when the service has critical dependencies (confidence
   `medium`). A liveness check must not call dependencies (WAFO-32); readiness must cover required dependencies only
   and return non-2xx on failure (WAFO-33). A single combined endpoint passes WAFO-34 when only one probe consumer is
   configured and startup is fast. Detailed diagnostics on an anonymous health route fail WAFO-37.
   OBS-07: SLOs count as documented when a target and its SLI are stated (README/docs, ADRs, OpenSLO/Sloth specs,
   SLO resources in IaC). A target without an SLI (e.g. only an SLA figure) fails with confidence `low` ("target
   without SLI"). Never fail OBS-07 for a library or CLI.
8. Evidence rule: fail only on concrete evidence in the files (e.g. an interpolated log message, an uninstrumented
   HTTP client in an instrumented app, a span with no end path, a metric attribute from a user ID, a console-only
   exporter in production config). Use confidence `medium` unless unambiguous; absence-only failures use `high` only
   if the language file's signals were searched across the whole file list.
9. Severity: every Finding takes the check's default severity from `checklist.md` regardless of element level;
   `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always that default.
10. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `OTO-01`); the report script derives `standard` and
    `url` from it, so don't write them.

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

### Checklist — Observability

Subject: Observability

Each check is evaluated against the local standards elements it lists (see `standards/`). Every element belongs to exactly one check.
Sources: OTO = `standards/opentelemetry-observability.md`; WAFO = `standards/azure-well-architected-observability.md`.

| id | Sub-subject | Check | Default severity | Elements | Source |
|----|-------------|-------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| OBS-01 | Structured Logging | Logging is structured (consistent schema, templates or key-value pairs, proper severity, shared framework), not free-text concatenation | Warning | OTO-01–OTO-06, WAFO-01–WAFO-03 | OTO, WAFO |
| OBS-02 | Correlation & Context Propagation | Correlation and trace context propagate across requests, async work and message boundaries, and logs carry trace IDs | Warning | OTO-07–OTO-11, WAFO-04–WAFO-05 | OTO, WAFO |
| OBS-03 | Distributed Tracing | Distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry SDK, zero-code agent or equivalent) covers inbound/outbound calls with correct span names, kinds and attributes | Warning | OTO-12–OTO-22, WAFO-06–WAFO-07 | OTO, WAFO |
| OBS-04 | Metrics | Metrics cover request rate, latency (histograms) and errors on key operations, plus business, job and async signals, with bounded cardinality | Warning | OTO-23–OTO-27, WAFO-08–WAFO-12 | OTO, WAFO |
| OBS-05 | Telemetry Export | Metrics, traces and logs are exported to a backend or collector through external configuration, not only to the local console | Information | OTO-28–OTO-30, WAFO-13 | OTO, WAFO |
| OBS-06 | Health Endpoints | Long-running services expose health endpoints wired to probes: shallow liveness, readiness that reflects required dependencies, cheap read-only checks, no anonymous diagnostic detail | Warning | WAFO-14–WAFO-18, WAFO-32–WAFO-37 | WAFO |
| OBS-07 | SLOs & SLIs | SLOs with measurable SLIs are documented for the service and its critical flows | Information | WAFO-19–WAFO-23 | WAFO |
| OBS-08 | Telemetry Identity & Naming | Telemetry identifies its source (`service.name`, version, environment, instance) and follows semantic-convention naming and UTC timestamps | Information | OTO-31–OTO-36, WAFO-24–WAFO-25 | OTO, WAFO |
| OBS-09 | Error Recording | Errors and exceptions are recorded correctly: span status and `error.type`, exception object logged once at an impact-based severity | Warning | OTO-37–OTO-43, WAFO-26 | OTO, WAFO |
| OBS-10 | Telemetry Volume & Safety | Telemetry volume and safety are controlled: configurable verbosity, deliberate sampling, non-blocking and failure-isolated instrumentation, no sensitive data in telemetry attributes or baggage | Information | OTO-44–OTO-46, WAFO-27–WAFO-31 | OTO, WAFO |

Totals: 46 OTO + 37 WAFO = 83 elements across 10 checks.

Alert rules, dashboards-as-code, external probes and telemetry-store settings are reviewed by `review-monitoring` (MON-01 … MON-06), which is N/A without IaC.

## File: `references/standards/opentelemetry-observability.md`

*Load rule: OTO-01…OTO-46. Always load.*

### OpenTelemetry — Application instrumentation — localized summary

- Licence: CC BY 4.0 (docs). Rows are summaries in our own words.
- Level: the strongest RFC 2119 keyword in the summarized sentences (`MUST`, `SHOULD`; lower-case "should"/"we recommend" on concept pages counts as `SHOULD`), otherwise `REVIEW`. Severity is always the owning check's default.
- Stab. column: `S` = stable; `D` = Development status in the pinned version. A `D` element applies only when the repo already uses that convention; otherwise report it only with confidence `low` and never above the check default.

#### OBS-01 — Logging is structured

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-01 | REVIEW | S | Logs use a consistent structured schema with stable field names and types. Valid JSON with varying fields isn't enough. | app emits logs |
| OTO-02 | REVIEW | S | Production code paths don't emit unstructured free text built by concatenation or interpolation; they use a standard logging framework with templates or key-value pairs. | app emits logs |
| OTO-03 | SHOULD | S | Application code logs through an established logging library bridged to OpenTelemetry by an appender/bridge; it doesn't call the Logs Bridge API (Logger, LoggerProvider) directly. | OpenTelemetry logs in use |
| OTO-04 | SHOULD | S | Log records carry a severity mapped consistently to TRACE/DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL. Error conditions are logged at ERROR or above, not INFO. | app emits logs |
| OTO-05 | SHOULD | S | Per-event context goes in attributes, not interpolated into the body. Well-known fields use semconv names. Event-shaped records use a stable event name. | app emits logs |
| OTO-06 | SHOULD | S | `IsEnabled`/`Enabled` guards are used only around costly argument evaluation, guarded code has no side effects, and the result is evaluated per record, not cached. | log guards present |

#### OBS-02 — Correlation and trace context propagate

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-07 | REVIEW | S | Logs emitted inside an active span carry TraceId and SpanId (through the SDK, appender or log-scope enrichment), so logs correlate with traces. | logs + tracing |
| OTO-08 | REVIEW | S | Context crosses process boundaries through propagators (inject on send, extract on receive). W3C Trace Context (`traceparent`) is the default; custom header schemes need a reason. | service calls or receives remote calls |
| OTO-09 | SHOULD | D | Message producers attach a creation context to each message. Consumers extract it and link to it (span links by default; parent only for single-message processing). | message broker in use |
| OTO-10 | REVIEW | S | In-process asynchronous work (threads, executors, background tasks, callbacks) carries the current context, so child spans attach to the right parent. | async or background work |
| OTO-11 | REVIEW | S | When context is carried in a custom protocol or payload, the receiver extracts it and removes it before processing. | custom carrier |

#### OBS-03 — Distributed tracing is instrumented

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-12 | REVIEW | S | Tracer, Meter and Logger providers are configured once at startup, live for the app's lifetime, and are given a Resource and exporters. They are never created per request. | code-based mode |
| OTO-13 | SHOULD | S | Tracers and meters are obtained from the provider and named after the instrumented component or library, with a version. | code-based mode |
| OTO-14 | REVIEW | S | Inbound and outbound frameworks (HTTP server and client, database, messaging) are covered by instrumentation libraries or a zero-code agent, not left uninstrumented. | service calls or receives remote calls |
| OTO-15 | SHOULD | S | Libraries depend only on the OpenTelemetry API. The SDK and exporters are wired only in the application. | library or multi-module repo |
| OTO-16 | REVIEW | S | Key business operations have custom spans with meaningful low-cardinality names. Every span is ended on all paths (finally/using/with) and sits under the correct parent. | custom spans present or business-critical flow |
| OTO-17 | REVIEW | S | Span kind matches direction: SERVER inbound, CLIENT outbound synchronous calls, PRODUCER/CONSUMER for queued jobs, INTERNAL for in-process work. | custom spans present |
| OTO-18 | MUST | S | HTTP span names are `{method} {http.route}` for servers (`{method}` or `url.template` for clients). The raw URI path is never the span name. | custom HTTP spans or naming config |
| OTO-19 | SHOULD | S | Custom HTTP spans carry the required attributes (method, route or path, scheme, status code; server address and port for clients). `http.route` is set at creation when known. | custom HTTP spans |
| OTO-20 | SHOULD | S | Custom DB spans use CLIENT kind and set `db.system.name` and the operation/collection. Query text is captured only parameterized or sanitized; parameter values are opt-in. | custom DB spans or DB instrumentation options |
| OTO-21 | SHOULD | D | Custom messaging spans are named `{operation} {destination}`, use the kind defined per operation, and set `messaging.system.name` and `messaging.operation.name`. | custom messaging spans |
| OTO-22 | REVIEW | S | Attributes are set at span start when available (for samplers) and use semconv names. Span events record timestamped occurrences; links record non-parent causal relations. | custom spans present |

#### OBS-04 — Metrics for request rate, latency and errors

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-23 | SHOULD | S | HTTP request duration is recorded as a histogram in seconds (`http.server.request.duration`, `http.client.request.duration`) or an equivalent RED metric; rate and errors derive from it. | HTTP service or client |
| OTO-24 | REVIEW | S | Each custom metric uses the fitting instrument: Counter (monotonic), UpDownCounter (in-flight, queue size), Histogram (durations, sizes), gauge (sampled state). Units follow semconv (`s`, `By`). | custom metrics present |
| OTO-25 | MUST | S | Metric attributes have bounded cardinality: no user, request or session IDs and no raw paths. Use route templates; unknown HTTP methods are reported as `_OTHER`. | metrics present |
| OTO-26 | REVIEW | S | Constant context (service, region, environment) is on the Resource, not repeated as an attribute on every metric. | metrics present |
| OTO-27 | REVIEW | S | Views that drop instruments, change aggregation or filter attributes are deliberate. Histogram buckets cover the service's latency range (semconv default 5 ms – 10 s). | views or bucket config present |

#### OBS-05 — Telemetry is exported to a backend

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-28 | REVIEW | S | Production configuration exports traces, metrics and logs over OTLP or a supported backend exporter. A console exporter is used only for development. | deployable service |
| OTO-29 | REVIEW | S | Exporter endpoint, protocol, headers and timeout come from configuration (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` or a config file), not hard-coded values; header credentials come from secret config. | exporter configured |
| OTO-30 | SHOULD | S | Production deployments send telemetry through a Collector (agent, sidecar or gateway) for batching, retries, encryption and filtering. Direct export is fine for development or small setups. | deployable service |

#### OBS-08 — Telemetry identity and naming

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-31 | MUST | S | `service.name` is set explicitly (`OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` or the Resource), is identical across instances of the service, and is never left as `unknown_service`. | telemetry SDK or agent in use |
| OTO-32 | REVIEW | S | `service.version` is set to the deployed artifact version (semver, build number or commit), not a constant. | telemetry SDK or agent in use |
| OTO-33 | REVIEW | D | `deployment.environment.name` (or the platform equivalent) is set from configuration per environment. | telemetry SDK or agent in use |
| OTO-34 | MUST | S | `service.namespace` groups related services where several share a name. `service.instance.id` is unique per instance (SDK or detector default is fine). | multi-service repo |
| OTO-35 | REVIEW | S | Resource detectors (host, container, Kubernetes, cloud) are enabled where available, instead of hand-coding host information into attributes. | code-based mode |
| OTO-36 | REVIEW | S | Custom telemetry names follow the semantic conventions (pinned version), not ad-hoc names. Semconv upgrades (`OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`) are adopted deliberately. | custom telemetry present |

#### OBS-09 — Errors and exceptions are recorded

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-37 | MUST | D | Failed operations set span status Error and `error.type`; successful ones leave status Unset (no blanket Ok). Status description is the exception message when not sensitive. | custom spans present |
| OTO-38 | MUST | S | HTTP status mapping: 5xx sets Error; 4xx sets Error on client spans only and stays Unset on server spans. Caller cancellation isn't an error. | custom HTTP spans or status mapping code |
| OTO-39 | SHOULD | D | Errors that were retried or handled aren't recorded as failures of that operation. A propagating exception is recorded once, not logged again at every layer. | error handling present |
| OTO-40 | MUST | S | Exceptions are logged with the exception object (type, message, stack trace), not only `ex.Message`, and within the active span's context. | exception logging present |
| OTO-41 | SHOULD | D | Exception severity reflects impact: FATAL process-ending, ERROR unhandled, WARN expected/handled, DEBUG cancellation. A global unhandled-exception handler logs at ERROR or FATAL. | exception logging present |
| OTO-42 | SHOULD | D | Duration metrics carry `error.type` on failure only, with the same value as the span. One metric covers success and failure (no separate failure counters). | custom metrics present |
| OTO-43 | SHOULD | D | Framework exceptions that only carry an HTTP status (e.g. `HTTPException`, `ResponseStatusException`) aren't recorded as exceptions. | such exceptions used |

#### OBS-10 — Telemetry volume, safety and configurability

| ID | Level | Stab. | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTO-44 | REVIEW | S | Sampling is a deliberate, configured policy (`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` or code). Default parent-based always-on is fine at low volume; high volume (≈ 1000+ traces/s) uses ratio and/or tail sampling keeping errors; nothing sampled where data mustn't drop. | tracing present |
| OTO-45 | MUST | S | Telemetry attributes hold no credentials or unneeded personal data: `url.full` has no user info and sensitive query values are redacted, headers/bodies aren't captured by default, user IDs are minimized or hashed. | tracing or metrics present |
| OTO-46 | REVIEW | S | Baggage carries no credentials, API keys or PII; context isn't propagated unfiltered to external services, and incoming context from untrusted sources is ignored or sanitized. | baggage used or external calls |

## File: `references/standards/azure-well-architected-observability.md`

*Load rule: WAFO-01…WAFO-37. Always load.*

### Azure Well-Architected Framework — Observability, health and reliability targets — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the pages use no normative keywords); severity is the owning check's default.
- Every element is Scope G (generic). No element depends on Azure services.

`oe-check` (OE:07) and `re-check` (RE:04, RE:10) are traceability only: OE:07 = design a monitoring system that captures operational telemetry; RE:04 = define reliability and recovery targets; RE:10 = measure and model the workload's health signals.

#### OBS-01 — Logging is structured

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-01 | REVIEW | One configurable logging framework (or a shared logging library) is used across components, with common schemas and naming conventions. | app emits logs |
| WAFO-02 | REVIEW | Telemetry is structured and both human- and machine-readable (JSON, MessagePack, Protobuf). | app emits logs |
| WAFO-03 | REVIEW | Events are logged at service boundaries: request start, duration and status, and dependency calls with duration, status, retries and errors. | service |

#### OBS-02 — Correlation and trace context propagate

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-04 | REVIEW | A correlation (activity) ID is generated at the entry point when absent and propagated when supplied, across services, threads, queues and dependencies. | service |
| WAFO-05 | REVIEW | Logs, metrics and traces share common identifiers across presentation, middle and data tiers. Correlation relies on IDs, not timestamps alone. | service |

#### OBS-03 — Distributed tracing is instrumented

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-06 | REVIEW | Instrumentation is vendor-neutral and language-agnostic (e.g. OpenTelemetry) and decoupled from a specific backend. | service |
| WAFO-07 | REVIEW | Distributed tracing covers the critical system flows end to end. | multi-service or dependency calls |

#### OBS-04 — Metrics for request rate, latency and errors

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-08 | REVIEW | Request-level signals (rate, duration, status) are emitted, and meaningful business events or KPIs (e.g. orders placed) are instrumented alongside technical metrics. | service |
| WAFO-09 | REVIEW | Latency is measured so that percentiles (p50/p95/p99) can be derived, not only averages. | service |
| WAFO-10 | REVIEW | Critical scheduled or background jobs emit both execution and result-validity signals (ran on schedule; output non-empty and well-formed). | scheduled jobs in code |
| WAFO-11 | REVIEW | Flows accepted synchronously and completed asynchronously emit acceptance and completion signals (backlog or message age). Fallback paths (e.g. cache miss → database) are observable. | async processing |
| WAFO-12 | REVIEW | Dependency retries and transient-fault occurrences are counted or logged. | retry policies present |

#### OBS-05 — Telemetry is exported to a backend

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-13 | REVIEW | Telemetry leaves local silos (local files, console) through a consistent collection method into a central store. No manual retrieval from components. | deployable service |

#### OBS-06 — Health endpoint exists

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-14 | REVIEW | Each deployable long-running service exposes a health endpoint that an external probe (load balancer, orchestrator, watchdog) can call. | long-running service |
| WAFO-15 | REVIEW | The health endpoint is wired to the host's probe mechanism (orchestrator probes, load-balancer health path, platform health-check setting) where those manifests are in scope. | deployment manifests in scope |
| WAFO-16 | REVIEW | Health checks measure responsiveness of the app and of its critical components and dependencies, and can report degraded as well as unhealthy rather than a constant OK. | service with critical dependencies |
| WAFO-17 | REVIEW | Health logic distinguishes transient from persistent faults, and a dependency with a working fallback degrades the result instead of failing it. | service with dependencies |
| WAFO-18 | REVIEW | Status APIs and admin summaries that the app exposes return fresh, accurate values. Stale cached state is detectable (e.g. a last-refreshed timestamp). | status API or admin summary in code |
| WAFO-32 | REVIEW | Liveness is a shallow check: it reports whether the process can respond and doesn't call downstream dependencies, so a dependency outage doesn't cause restarts. | liveness endpoint or probe present |
| WAFO-33 | REVIEW | Readiness is a deep check of initialization and the dependencies required to serve requests; it returns non-2xx (e.g. 503) when a required check fails. Optional dependencies don't fail it. | service with required dependencies |
| WAFO-34 | REVIEW | Consumers that need different signals get separate endpoints or check groups (liveness vs readiness; core vs lower-priority services). Startup time is allowed for, not treated as failure. | more than one probe consumer, or slow startup |
| WAFO-35 | REVIEW | Health checks are bounded and cheap: a timeout per dependency check, degraded status or circuit breaker for unreliable dependencies, no heavy work per probe. A cached result's TTL fits the detection delay. | health checks call dependencies |
| WAFO-36 | REVIEW | Health checks are read-only: they don't change production data or trigger downstream workflows. A synthetic transaction that must write uses isolated test accounts and data. | health checks present |
| WAFO-37 | REVIEW | Anonymous health responses return only the status a probe needs. Detailed diagnostics (dependency names, versions, error text) require authorization. An obscure path or port isn't access control. | health endpoint present |

#### OBS-07 — SLOs or SLIs are documented

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-19 | REVIEW | Reliability targets are documented: SLOs for the workload and its critical flows, each measurable through stated SLIs within a stated observability window. | deployable service |
| WAFO-20 | REVIEW | SLIs cover success rate, percentile latency and availability, plus throughput or capacity where they apply. | SLOs stated |
| WAFO-21 | REVIEW | SLOs are kept distinct from SLAs. A platform SLA isn't adopted as an SLO without checking its coverage, and critical dependencies are included in composite targets. | SLOs or SLAs stated |
| WAFO-22 | REVIEW | SLO scope fits the deployment: per tenant for multitenant SaaS, per stamp for bulkhead multi-region deployments. | multitenant or multi-stamp |
| WAFO-23 | REVIEW | Business KPIs are defined alongside technical SLIs, and SLIs map to health states (healthy / degraded / unhealthy definitions). | SLOs stated |

#### OBS-08 — Telemetry identity and naming

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-24 | REVIEW | Telemetry consistently records source component, environment, deployment/version and operation name, plus tenant or user ID only where allowed. | telemetry present |
| WAFO-25 | REVIEW | Timestamps are taken when the event occurs and recorded in a universal format (UTC). | telemetry present |

#### OBS-09 — Errors and exceptions are recorded

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-26 | REVIEW | Critical exceptions and failures are logged with enough detail for diagnosis (exception information, operation, dependency). | error handling present |

#### OBS-10 — Telemetry volume, safety and configurability

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAFO-27 | REVIEW | Log verbosity is configurable per environment without a code change, levels are used properly, and high-volume components sample. | app emits logs |
| WAFO-28 | REVIEW | Logging is asynchronous (fire-and-forget) and kept off the request path, except where audit requires synchronous writes. | app emits logs |
| WAFO-29 | REVIEW | Telemetry failures (exporter or backend unavailable) don't cascade into application failures. Buffers are bounded and errors are contained. | telemetry SDK in use |
| WAFO-30 | REVIEW | Telemetry is classified by concern (audit, security, diagnostic, performance). Audit logs are kept separate from diagnostic logs; workload data isn't written into telemetry. | app emits logs |
| WAFO-31 | REVIEW | Telemetry-specific sensitive data is scrubbed before export while diagnostic context is kept. (Secrets/PII in log messages belong to the security skills.) | telemetry present |
